entries.reason: test_TEST_027_receiverRuleRefusesEveryClass fills an array of receivers that must all be refused and checks each; removing one assignment leaves that element address(0), which is itself in the refused set, so the loop still passes. The original test does check every listed receiver; Necessist's removal only replaces one refused value by another.

Independence tests: the test pins that an action is NOT affected by a hostile or stopped environment (a broken registry or RiskModule, a frozen wallet, a paused Hub, another Hub's pause, an approve-all RiskModule, a halted Spoke), and sets several such conditions at once. Removing one of them leaves the action in a less hostile environment, where it must pass too; the statement is what makes the test meaningful, but its removal cannot make a correct implementation fail. Selected by the setter (setBroken(true), setFrozen(.., true), a Paused/Frozen pause, setApproveAll(true), _setHalted(.., true), _setState) in a test whose name states the independence (Ignores, Still, Never, NoEffect, OtherHub, InEveryPauseState, WithBroken, ReadsNoRegistry, ...).

entries.reason: AaveAdapter.repay is open to any payer (REQ-ADAPT repay by anyone, TEST-165): the call gives the same result whether the payer is carol or the test contract, so the prank is not needed for the zero-debt and zero-cap cases these tests pin.

test_TEST_108_constructorFailsClosed builds seven bad configurations with (badN[i], badF[i]) = (n, f). badN and badF are address[4][7] memory, whose rows are memory pointers, so this assignment makes every row a reference to the same n and f arrays rather than a copy. Each later corruption (badN[0][3] = 0, badF[1][0] = 0, badN[2][1] = alice, ...) therefore writes into n or f and appears in all seven rows at once, and the final 'stray manager' case (n[3] = stray) still carries alice and the swapped managers. Every deployment is refused because of several faults together, so no single constructor rule is checked on its own and removing any one corruption (or the fill loop) leaves the test passing.
entries.strengthen: Copy element by element (for j < 4: badN[i][j] = n[j]; badF[i][j] = f[j]), keep n and f unmodified for the stray case (use a fresh copy), and add a positive control first: new SlipstreamIntegration(1, coll, registry, l, timelock, n, f) succeeds with the untouched lists. Then each of the seven expectRevert(InvalidDeployment) cases differs from a deployable configuration by exactly one fault.

entries.reason: testFuzz_TEST_219_servedByStateBothRoutes draws p and b as independent uint40 values, so the agreeing branch (|p - b| within TOLERANCE = 225 bps, expected = p) and the both-invalid branch (p and b each 0 or >= 1e12, expected = A) are almost never reached: removing the expected value of either branch (expected stays 0, which assertEq(served, expected) would refuse) left the test passing. The test names both routes' states but checks the Live/agreeing and no-valid-route cases only by chance.
entries.strengthen: Steer the inputs: in a share of the runs derive b from p inside the tolerance (b = p +- bound(delta, 0, p * 225 / 1e4)) and in another share make both answers invalid (0 or >= 1e12), or split the branches into their own fuzz tests, so assertEq(served, p) and assertEq(served, a) run every campaign.

entries.reason: testFuzz_TEST_036_lpPriceMalformedNeverReverts draws na, nv and nd independently in [0, 10], so equal lengths in [2, 8] (the only case where element bounds matter) occur in about 0.5 % of runs. Removing the element-bound update of inBounds (which would make the expectation wrong for any equal-length case with an out-of-range element) left the test passing: the element checks of lpPrice (amount < 2^128, 1 <= price <= MAX_ROUTE, decimals <= 77) are rarely exercised by this test.
entries.strengthen: Draw one length for all three arrays in most runs (for example nv = nd = na unless a separate flag asks for mismatched lengths), so assertEq(valid, inBounds) runs on equal-length compositions with out-of-range elements in every campaign.

entries.reason: testFuzz_TEST_251_usdBandIsTheFixedPointTest draws high uniformly in [low, 1e18] while the capped product pv is at most 1e8 per token, so the upper band test (pv <= fixedPointPower(high, n)) is true in almost every run. Removing the multiplication that builds pv (leaving only v[0]) left the test passing: the upper bound of the band is not checked near its boundary.

entries.reason: testFuzz_TEST_078_settlementMatchesModel: without p.maxShortfall = maxShortfall the call carries maxShortfall 0, every run that needs a top-up reverts RecoveryBelowFloor, and the catch accepts that error on any run. The test passed, so it does not check that a shortfall within the budget settles as the model says (the model is even called with the fuzzed budget).
entries.strengthen: In the catch branch, accept RecoveryBelowFloor only when the modelled floor gap (minRec - R) exceeds p.maxShortfall; and add a fixed case with a non-zero shortfall within the budget that must settle with r.shortfall equal to the model's gap.

entries.reason: testFuzz_TEST_078_waterfallWithTopUp: without p.maxShortfall = debtToCover / 10 the call carries maxShortfall 0, every run that needs a top-up reverts RecoveryBelowFloor, and the catch accepts it. The test named for the top-up passed without any top-up settling.
entries.strengthen: In the catch branch accept RecoveryBelowFloor only when the modelled floor gap exceeds p.maxShortfall, and assert that at least one fixed input settles with r.shortfall > 0.

entries.reason: test_TEST_055_invalidAmounts states that a two-entry minimum is accepted and passed to Collateralization, and sets minAmounts[1] = 1 for that. Without it the minimums are [0, 0] and the test still passes: nothing checks that the minimums reach Collateralization.settleSeizure.
entries.strengthen: Add vm.expectCall(address(coll), abi.encodeCall(ICollateralization.settleSeizure, (proxy, address(vt), expectedUnits, p.minAmounts))) before the liquidation, or assert a release minimum above the amount is refused with its exact error.

entries.reason: testFuzz_TEST_078_ghoSettlementMatchesModel: without p.maxShortfall = maxShortfall the call carries maxShortfall 0, every run that needs a top-up reverts RecoveryBelowFloor, and the catch accepts that error on any run. The test passed, so it does not check that a GHO shortfall within the budget settles as the model says.
entries.strengthen: In the catch branch accept RecoveryBelowFloor only when the modelled floor gap exceeds p.maxShortfall (and NoRouteAvailable only when a route is down), so a refused top-up within the budget fails the test.

entries.reason: testFuzz_TEST_071_noOverflowInTheDebtUnitConversions asserts only that a failed liquidate did not revert with Panic. Without _fund (or with the test contract as caller after removing the prank) every run reverts in _fund's transferFrom with an ERC20 error before any debt-unit conversion runs, and the test still passes: it never shows that the conversions it names were reached.
entries.strengthen: Assert that the call succeeds when the account is liquidatable (ok == true, or ok || the revert selector is one of the named LPVaultSwap errors), so a run that stops at funding fails the test.

entries.reason: test_TEST_247_pledgeAfterKeepsTheAccountsFactorAndFirstPledgeTakesTheLatest: Bob's half claims a first pledge moves the account to the latest collateral factor, but Bob has no debt, so every value asserted for him (collateralValueAfter $2,000, healthFactorAfter = max, and _assertAfter's health factor, debt value, collateral value and liquidation price) is independent of the collateral factor and of the Adapter stand-in knowing his proxy. Removing the new 60 % factor (U1750) or Bob's bind (U1751) still passed. Alice's half (HF 8e18 at the account's own 80 %) is pinned.
entries.strengthen: Give Bob a debt after his first pledge (e.g. borrow 500 GHO as bobProxy) and assert the Spoke's health factor is 2,000 x 0.6 / 500 = 2.4e18, or preview a borrow for Bob and assert its healthFactorAfter uses 60 %.

entries.reason: Paging fuzz tests (getRecords / checkRecordBacking): `offset` and `limit` are unbounded uint256, so apart from the fuzzer's few small edge values every run takes the `limit > 200` revert branch or has offset >= count, where the expected page length is 0 whatever records exist. Removing the `_open` loop (no records at all) still passed: the test does not reliably pin `min(limit, n - offset)` on a non-empty page.
entries.strengthen: Bound `offset` to [0, count + 2] and `limit` to [0, 210] (keeping the > 200 revert case), and assert r.length > 0 whenever offset < count and limit > 0, so the page-size formula and (for checkRecordBacking) the `backed` loop run on real records.

entries.reason: test_TEST_027_recommendedAndMaximumBorrow claims that a borrow of 14,183.23 USDC ends at or above health 1.10 and that 15,601.56 USDC is the protocol maximum at 1.00. The only assertion after each borrow is a lower bound on the proxy's health factor, which also holds with no debt at all, so the test passes without the borrow it describes; only the borrow's own non-revert carries the claim.
entries.strengthen: After each _borrowTo assert the proxy's USDC debt equals the borrowed amount (assertEq(_debtOf(proxy, usdcReserveId), 14_183_230_000) and 15_601_560_000) and bound the health factor from above as well (for the maximum row, assertLt(_hf(proxy), 1.1e18) or the exact floored value).

entries.reason: testFuzz_TEST_047_minAmountsAtTheRelease expects a refusal when one minimum is one above the release amount, with a bare vm.expectRevert(). The release minimum is checked in settleSeizure, after _fund; without _fund the call reverts in transferFrom for lack of funds, the bare expectRevert accepts it, and the test still passes, so the refusal by the release minimum is not pinned.
entries.strengthen: Expect the exact revert data of the release-minimum check (the LPVault/Collateralization error raised by settleSeizure for an amount below its minimum) instead of a bare vm.expectRevert().

entries.reason: test_TEST_248_feeOnTransferRepayAllReverts funds alice so that a repay-all with a fee-on-transfer token is refused for the short delivery, but uses a bare vm.expectRevert(). Without the funding alice has no balance or allowance and the pull reverts for that reason; the bare expectRevert accepts it, so the test does not pin the fee-on-transfer refusal.
entries.strengthen: Expect the exact error the adapter raises for the short delivery (BalanceDeltaMismatch or the repay-all shortfall error) instead of vm.expectRevert().

entries.reason: test_TEST_042_burningSourceFailsStarvedCallerReverts claims that the per-read gas guard refuses a caller with too little gas (InsufficientGas) while a source that burns its explicit gas fails the market. _lowerFloor sets pokeMinGas to 1 so that the 120,000-gas poke reaches the reads. Without it pokeMinGas stays 900,000 and the 120,000-gas call is refused by the entry check before any read; the test only asserts ok == false and that storage is unchanged, so it passes without ever reaching the per-read guard.
entries.strengthen: After (ok,) = _poke(120_000) keep ret and assert bytes4(ret) == ILPOracleErrors.InsufficientGas.selector, decode (left, required) as in test_TEST_042_floorIsGasLeftAtTheEntryCheck, and assertLt(required, 900_000) (or assertEq(required, <the read's pre-call bound>)) so the refusal is shown to come from a read's bound, not from pokeMinGas.

entries.reason: test_TEST_048_callerTransferFailureReverts funds the keeper so that the only fault is the token returning false, then expects a revert with a bare vm.expectRevert(). Without _fund the keeper has no balance or allowance and the call reverts in the pull for that reason; the bare expectRevert accepts it, so the test does not show that a false return is refused.
entries.strengthen: Expect the exact data, vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(SafeERC20.SafeERC20FailedOperation.selector, address(usdc))), for the return-false case.

entries.reason: test_TEST_098_frozenOperatorsAreNotActive removes the frozen carol and asserts 'the frozen one removed' with activeKeeperCount() == 1. A frozen operator is never counted as active, so the count is 1 with or without the removal; the test passed without _remove(carol), so the removal's effect is not checked.
entries.strengthen: After _remove(carol) assert lvs.approvedKeeperCount() == 1 and assertFalse(lvs.isApprovedKeeper(carol)).

entries.reason: test_TEST_228_latchedEventCarriesTheWholeSet first latches ISSUER and then expects BreakerLatched(ISSUER | CONFIG_DRIFT), but the second report itself carries CONFIG_DRIFT | ISSUER. Without the first latch the second report emits the same event, so the test does not distinguish 'the event carries the whole latched set' from 'the event carries the security bits of this report'.
entries.strengthen: Make the second report carry only CONFIG_DRIFT (recordBreach(mKey, BreakerReasons.CONFIG_DRIFT)) and keep the expected BreakerLatched(Market, mKey, ISSUER | CONFIG_DRIFT).

entries.reason: test_TEST_042_pokeReturnsTheReportedState claims that poke() returns the reported state in every state (Live, Drifting by disagreement, by the band, by an unavailable consistency check, Cached by the pool lock, Cached by the quote-change cap, Expired). The helper _assertPokeMatchesReport only compares poke() with getPriceState() from the same snapshot; the label is the assert message and the expected state is never asserted. Removing the statement that creates a state (or resets the previous one) leaves the test comparing two equal states of some other kind, so the test does not show it reached each named state.
entries.strengthen: Give _assertPokeMatchesReport an expected PriceState argument and add assertEq(uint8(v.state), uint8(expected), label) before the poke (Live, Drifting, Drifting, Drifting, Cached, Cached, Expired in order); for the quote-cap and lock cases also assert the reason bit (QUOTE_CHANGE_CAPPED bit 18, POOL_REENTRANCY_LOCKED).

entries.reason: Three tests whose names or NatSpec say a residue the helper cannot receive is escrowed for the helper in the PayoutEscrow and claimed to the caller in the same call (FlashLiquidator.Funding test_TEST_289_publicHelperCreditGoesToItsCaller, FlashLiquidator.unit test_TEST_289_residueRefusedByHelperEscrowedToHelper, FlashLiquidator.Residues test_TEST_174_escrowedIntermediateClaimedToTheCaller) still pass without the token's setBlocked(helper, true). MockLiquidationSwap then transfers the residue to the helper directly, the helper forwards it, and the assertions (claimable 0, the caller holds the residue, feeRecipient 0) hold. None of them shows that the escrow credit was created and claimed.
entries.strengthen: Before the liquidation add vm.expectEmit(address(escrow)); emit RemainderEscrowed(token, address(helper), amount); and vm.expectEmit(address(escrow)); emit RemainderClaimed(token, address(helper), caller, amount); (or vm.expectCall(address(escrow), abi.encodeWithSelector(IPayoutEscrow.claim.selector))), so a direct payment fails the test.

entries.reason: testFuzz_TEST_218_cascadeLiquidatesEveryEligibleAccount drops the vault price of both markets (lpOracle for market 4, lpOracleB for market 5); every account starts at HF 1.10. Without one of the two setAnswer calls that market's six accounts stay healthy, and the positive control (settledCount > 0 when dropBps > 1000) is summed over both markets, so it is met by the other market alone. The test passed without a cascade in one market.
entries.strengthen: Count settled liquidations per market and assert each count is > 0 when dropBps > 1000 (or assert that at least one account of each market was eligible before the loop).

entries.reason: test_TEST_233_shortfallThroughHelper sets both USDT/USDC pools to 0.95 so the recovery falls below the floor and the caller's 200e6 budget tops it up. No assertion checks that a shortfall occurred (payout to the caller, keeperOut above the loan, nothing left in the helper all hold without one), so the test passed with either pool at its fixture rate.

bound() in a fuzz test only maps the generated input into the domain the property is stated for (the ranges named in the test, its NatSpec or the function's documented input limits).
